result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (4/4 tests green).

## Summary

Applied the framework's existing `createRateLimitMiddleware` (from `@guren/core`, re-exported from `@guren/server`) to the `POST /login` route only, in `routes/auth.ts`. It's configured with `limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000`, no `trustProxy` (default `false`), so it keys attempts by the raw connection IP via `server.requestIP()` and never trusts `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP`-style headers; if the IP can't be resolved it falls back to a single shared bucket rather than skipping the check, satisfying the fail-closed requirement. The counter is in-memory (`MemoryRateLimitStore`, the library's default), increments on every submission whether or not credentials are valid, and returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header once exceeded — all built into the library middleware, so `LoginController` needed no changes. The middleware is attached only to the `POST /login` route (as a trailing route-level middleware, which the router runs after the `guest` alias but before the controller/body validation), so `GET /login`, registration, and every other route are untouched.

Added `tests/LoginRateLimit.test.ts`, which boots the real app via `TestApp`, primes CSRF, sends 5 login POSTs and confirms none are throttled, confirms the 6th (and a subsequent) request returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header, and confirms `GET /login`, `/`, and `/posts` remain unaffected while throttled.
